title: Key Stability Scorecard and TTL Rollback Automation
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Background: Our autotune experiments show non-uniform prefix stability across customers. Some prefixes produce volatile hit rates after config changes, causing cost regressions when TTLs are increased or when keys are coalesced. Current rollout tooling can apply TTL/policy changes but lacks an automated, model-driven guardrail that detects unstable key groups and triggers a safe rollback.

Objective: Build a Key Stability Scorecard and an automated TTL rollback system that: 1) scores prefix/key groups for stability based on historical hit-rate variance, request fanout, and sample entropy; 2) integrates with the shadow-canary dry-run harness to estimate impact before production apply; 3) automatically reverts changes when post-apply stability < threshold or when cost/latency regressions exceed SLOs; 4) produces actionable recommendations for key reshaping and per-prefix TTL adjustments.

Deliverables: 
- Stability scoring prototype (notebook + production inference function) that outputs a per-prefix score (0-1) and explanatory features.
- A policy mapping: score buckets -> suggested TTL delta, coalescing rules, and canary sizes.
- Shadow-canary integration: run simulated cache with production traces and the candidate policy to produce expected hit-rate and cost delta.
- Automated rollback operator: a controller that watches rollout metrics, evaluates stability post-apply, and triggers rollback if thresholds are breached.
- Documentation and runbook: how to interpret the scorecard, manual override steps, and postmortem checklist.

Acceptance criteria: 
- Scorecard precision: in A/B tests, prefixes flagged as "unstable" should contain >= 80% of cases that showed hit-rate drop > 10% after naive TTL bump experiments.
- Rollback automation: when triggered, rollback must complete within 5 minutes and return hit-rate/latency to pre-apply baselines within 15 minutes for 95% of incidents.
- Cost impact: pilot on 3 customers reduces per-token cost by at least 6% net (after accounting for rollbacks and canary traffic).
- Observability: Console dashboard tile showing score distribution, active rollouts with triggers, and recent rollback events.

Approach: 
1) Data modeling: combine prefix-level time series of hit_rate, requests, distinct-user entropy, and key churn to train a lightweight explicable model (gradient-boosted tree) producing the stability score. Model will be validated in notebook and exported as a simplified scoring function for the runtime (to avoid heavy deps).
2) Simulation: reuse the shadow-canary harness to replay 72h of recent traces and compare candidate policy vs baseline. Report simulated net-token savings, mean hit-rate delta, and 95th percentile latency.
3) Policy design: generate a mapping table from score buckets to safe TTL deltas (e.g., score>=0.8 => +20% TTL, 0.6-0.8 => +10% TTL with small canary, <0.6 => no change + recommendation to reshape keys).
4) Rollout controller: implement a controller in the deployment service that watches canary metrics (hit-rate, tail-latency, inferred cost) and runs evaluation checks at 1m, 5m, and 15m marks. If conditions fail, controller invokes rollback API and annotates the rollout with the triggering signal.
5) Safety controls: require manual approval for any policy causing >15% simulated cost delta and add a forced dry-run stage for low-volume customers.

Trade-offs and decisions: 
- We prioritize explainability over marginal model accuracy to keep scoring runtime-light and debuggable.
- Conservative thresholds initially to avoid customer impact; may tune after pilot.
- Will not attempt automated key re-canonization in this phase — only TTL and coalescing suggestions.

Risks: 
- Score miscalibration could under- or over-trigger rollbacks. Mitigation: offline backtests + manual review for first 6 rollouts.
- Simulation fidelity: shadow replay may not capture downstream KV cache interactions for some customers. Mitigation: require small production canaries before full apply.

Rollout plan: 
- Week 1-2: data collection and scorecard prototype (notebook).
- Week 3: integrate score into shadow-canary and run 2 weeks of replays across 5 customers.
- Week 5: implement rollout controller with rollback hooks; internal end-to-end test on staging.
- Week 6: pilot on 3 customers with manual monitors and on-call coverage.
- Post-pilot: refine thresholds and promote to broader rollout.

Links: confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CO/Key+Stability+Scorecard, prototype notebook: s3://redwood-internal/experiments/stability-scorecard/nb_v1.ipynb, example runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7924

Notes for reviewers: please focus review on the scoring features and the proposed 3-stage check windows for the controller. PM and Solutions should confirm acceptable customer impact tolerances before pilot.
comments: 2025-02-12 Lina Chen: Scoping completed. Notebook prototype ingesting 14 days of prefix traces exists at s3://redwood-internal/experiments/stability-scorecard/nb_v1.ipynb. Initial features: hit_rate_ts, req_qps, distinct_user_entropy, prefix_cardinality_change. \nNext: define labeling heuristic for unstable prefixes (pre/post apply deltas).

2025-02-18 Theo Patel: Prototype model (LightGBM) trained on 20k prefixes. Offline precision@recall looks promising: recall 0.84, precision 0.72 for unstable class on holdout. Pushing scoring function to simplified rule: top 4 features weighted to avoid heavy runtime deps.

2025-02-24 Marcus Rivera (PM): Reviewed acceptance criteria. Requested addition of cost-simulation numbers in shadow-canary report and a soft throttle to cap daily rollout volume to 10% of customer's traffic during pilot.

2025-02-28 Ava Martinez (Design): UX mockups for Console tile and per-rollout drilldown uploaded to Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/Redwood/scorecard-console. Requested that rollback event include 'stability reason' string for quick root cause triage.

2025-03-03 Theo Patel: Implemented controller checks and a staging end-to-end with synthetic traffic. Observed forced rollback on 2/5 synthetic policies due to latency tail spike; investigating whether spike is from coalescing logic or simulation artifact. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7924

2025-03-05 Lina Chen: Decided thresholds: auto-rollback if simulated hit-rate delta < -0.06 OR 95th-latency regresses > 20% OR cost increases > 8% compared to baseline. These thresholds are conservative and will be tuned after pilot.\n
